narrative: Fifteen months of recurring, quickly-patched failures across nearly every module - connectors, dashboards, exports, API, report builder - with the same faults resurfacing months apart ('same symptoms as back in June', 'third time this has happened'). Support fixes fast (mostly 1-2 days) and the account keeps reporting calmly rather than threatening to leave, but the underlying instability is never actually solved, just re-patched. Worth a root-cause review before fatigue turns into departure.
Single ticket about adding seats for a new office - a routine expansion question, promptly answered. No friction, no history to judge trajectory against; this reads as a healthy, growing account.

Connector, API and alerting failures accumulated through the second half of 2024 into a formal escalation in April 2025 ('this isn't a one-off, it's a pattern... it needs a named owner'), after which the account explicitly credits the team: 'Your team has been responsive since the escalation, appreciated.' The only open item by October is a trivial seat-count mismatch and a feature request, both non-urgent. Textbook recovery - anger, escalation, genuine fix, calm follow-through.
Two spaced-out configuration questions - cross-team alerts, seat role permissions - each resolved within a week with no complaint. No history of friction; a quiet, healthy account.

A steady run of build-out questions over nine months - export API automation, JSON/CSV export consistency, template version control, dashboard embedding, API pagination limits - each answered without complaint. The account is actively deepening its use of the platform (building an automated pipeline, embedding dashboards), which is a growth signal, not a risk signal.

A run of finance-critical failures (delayed alerts, a year-end export gap, connector and export breakage) culminated in an April 2025 formal escalation demanding senior contact. The next ticket confirms it worked ('there's been more contact from your side, which I appreciate') and every ticket since - seat cleanup, audit access, a feature question - is routine and cooperative. Risk has fallen sharply since the escalation was honoured.

Four spaced-out how-to and configuration questions over seven months - connector setup, report scheduling, role permissions, seat transfer - each resolved within a week. No complaints, no repeat issues, no signs of friction. A quietly healthy, actively-expanding account.

competitor_mentions.quote: We looked briefly at Storsund BI's export logging as a point of comparison while thinking this through.

narrative: Only three tickets in six months, but the substance is the warning: a request for export-failure monitoring goes unmet, silent export failures then actually happen ('we only noticed because the files were missing from the shared drive'), and by May the account has simply built its own monitoring script rather than wait on the platform ('we're covered regardless of what happens on the platform side'). A new dashboard lag is explicitly deprioritised ('this isn't high priority for us to chase further'), alongside a passing comparison to Storsund BI's export logging. Quiet resignation, not stability - the sparse volume is masking a customer that has stopped expecting fixes.

A steady run of setup and expansion questions over ten months - a custom Postgres connector, SSO rollout, API access, dashboard performance at scale - with a satisfied follow-up on SSO ('working well since we set it up last month'). All resolved without complaint. A textbook healthy, growing account.

competitor_mentions.quote: We had a look at how Dashlume handles this during a broader tooling review this quarter, mainly to understand what's realistic to expect from a platform at this level.
Our tooling review, which has touched on Dashlume among others, continues in the background, but nothing is being decided in a hurry.

narrative: Four tickets across thirteen months look harmless until you read them: a retention question never gets a firm answer so the account builds its own archive instead, a persistent month-end dashboard delay gets worked around rather than escalated ('our finance team has adjusted timing around it rather than waiting'), and a report-builder feature question surfaces an active, ongoing tooling review that has 'touched on Dashlume among others.' Nothing is angry and nothing demands escalation, but the account is quietly building independence from the platform and comparison-shopping in parallel - the exact low-volume, high-risk pattern.

A clean sequence of expansion questions as the account onboards a new subsidiary - connector setup, seat licensing, consolidated exports, currency conversion, schedule changes, restricted dashboard access. Every ticket is a forward-looking configuration question, none a complaint, all resolved quickly. Healthy, growing account with no friction on record.

Eighteen tickets over sixteen months show a genuinely high defect rate - a report-builder save error that keeps returning ('the recurring save error is back... I've stopped being surprised at this point'), an admin role-revert bug that resurfaces months later on a different user, and repeat dashboard and alert failures - but every one gets fixed in 1-2 days and the account keeps filing tickets rather than going quiet. Volume and irritation are high, but engagement stays high too; the resignation in tone is worth watching but hasn't yet translated into pulling back.

A serious reliability crisis - recurring connector and export failures from January through July 2025, a 30-day export queue outage, and a formal escalation demanding account-manager involvement ('five tickets, most requiring workarounds rather than fixes') - is followed by an explicit, credible fix: 'the export queue has been stable all week since the patch went in... appreciate someone finally sorting the seat count.' Every ticket after early September is minor and fast-turnaround, including a good-natured feature suggestion from 'someone who's spent too long staring at that queue this year.' Real damage happened, but the recovery is genuine and recent.

An API token expiry bug (11 days to fix) and a NetSuite OAuth setup failure (6 days) were real but isolated friction early on; the account then moves straight to a routine seat-expansion request for its Enterprise plan with no further complaint. The growth signal outweighs the early friction.

Six distinct, unrelated technical issues in three months - connector sync, a currency display bug, an oversized-table crash in report builder, and a 13-day SSO lockout affecting the finance team - each reported and resolved factually with no repeat occurrences or anger. This is a normal rate of platform friction for an active account, not a pattern of recurring, unresolved faults.

Four spaced-out, unrelated tickets over eight months - offboarding, a formula bug, a report-builder default, alerts landing in spam - each a one-off, resolved without complaint or repeat. A low-friction, healthy account.

Four distinct issues over sixteen months - missing CSV headers, an alert distribution list update, an export timeout on a growing dataset, and an overnight refresh failure - each resolved within a week with no complaint about repeat occurrence. Ordinary account maintenance, not a pattern of unresolved risk.

Ville Lehtinen's account is methodically documented and shows a genuine pattern: an API documentation gap that went unaddressed for months, and an export timeout that recurred three times ('Third time we have raised this. Still not fixed.') despite each occurrence being marked resolved. A December 2024 escalation demanded someone 'with the authority to fix it, not just acknowledge it.' The most recent ticket (April 2025) is a calm, routine formula question with no mention of the prior problems - a good sign, but nothing in the record confirms the export issue was ever root-caused rather than patched again.

A small team absorbed a genuinely bad stretch - export, alert-timing, API and report-builder failures through March 2025 escalating to 'need someone senior to actually own our account' and, months later, still unresolved connector failures ('we can't keep absorbing this'). Since July the tone flips decisively: the formatting bug 'hasn't recurred since the July fix,' the new account contact is 'really responsive,' and the account is now asking for a Slack alert feature while praising stability. A genuine, credited turnaround.

Only three tickets in eight months, but the second pair tells the real story: warehouse connector sync gaps reported in August 2024 are still present two months later ('haven't really gone away'), and rather than push for a fix the account has built a parallel Excel reconciliation log and explicitly stopped chasing it ('not chasing a fix with any urgency... wanted to close the loop on our end regardless'). No anger, no escalation - just quiet acceptance that the platform's data can't be fully trusted, with a manual workaround absorbing the gap.
